title: Fan-out bound counts stamped rows, not sends, and is snapshot-racy — '3 emails/recipient/hour' is not actually enforced
evidence:
-- (max 3 continue emails per recipient per hour across ALL vacancies: the
-- endpoint is public, so without this an attacker sprays branded Resend
-- email at a victim from many vacancies).
...
SET continue_token = COALESCE(continue_token, $3),
    last_link_sent_at = now()
...
  AND (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d2
    WHERE d2.email = lower($2)
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at IS NOT NULL
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
  ) < 3
detail: Two holes in the round-2 W6 fix: (a) repeat sends re-stamp the SAME row, so the distinct-row count never grows — one vacancy can email a victim every 10 min (6/hr), two vacancies 12/hr; (b) READ COMMITTED snapshot means concurrent claims across different vacancy rows all see the pre-burst count and pass, so N simultaneous continue-link POSTs (free signup, ≤20 unpaid vacancies; the same request upserts the draft) deliver N branded emails at once.
recommended_fix: Serialize the claim per recipient (e.g. pg_advisory_xact_lock on hashtext(lower(email))) and count SEND EVENTS (a send-log table or a sends_in_hour counter incremented per claim), not distinct stamped rows.

title: 500/vacancy draft cap is attacker-consumable and racy — burning it silently disables save-and-resume for real applicants
evidence:
OR (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  ) < 500
ON CONFLICT (vacancy_id, email) DO UPDATE
...and in draft_handler.gleam handle_save_draft: "Ok(_) -> { ... wisp.json_response(json_ok(True), 200) }" (zero-row upsert still answers ok:true).
detail: The count includes tombstoned/stripped rows and the endpoint has no edge rate limit (Cloudflare rule is a deferred 'Ask First' item), so an unauthenticated attacker with the public vacancy code can burn all 500 slots with throwaway emails; afterwards legitimate saves silently no-op until vacancy close. The snapshot-based count also lets concurrent inserts exceed 500. Submissions themselves are unaffected.
recommended_fix: Exclude tombstoned/stripped rows from the cap count (WHERE submitted_at IS NULL AND erased_at IS NULL) and surface cap rejection distinctly (e.g. ok:false, cap:true) so monitoring can see it; keep the deferred edge rate limit on the roadmap.
